Santander (www.santander.com) is evolving from a global, high-impact brand into a technology-driven organisation, and our people are at the heart of this journey. THE AI ACCELERATOR 

Most diseases are still poorly understood at a biological level. Despite decades of research, the causal mechanisms driving many conditions remain unclear, limiting our ability to identify the right targets, design the right interventions and bring the right medicines to patients. 

The AI Accelerator exists to change that. Based in London and sitting within Computational Innovation (@computationalinnovation), a global organisation spanning computational biology, human genetics, data excellence and AI, the Accelerator’s mission is to build production-quality AI capabilities that deepen our understanding of disease biology and increase probability of success.  

We do this by applying neural-based methods across the biomedical data landscape to integrate heterogeneous, multimodal data sources, infer biological relationships and embed causal thinking into what we build. The goal is not just to predict but to explain and understand why disease occurs. 

It could be electronic health records and medical imaging to support patient segmentation. It could be ‘omics data to identify novel therapeutic targets. It could be predicting transcriptional change for a given disease-causing variant. It could be simulating the effect of modulating a target of interest. 

A core component of the AI Accelerator is AI Systems, a team focused on designing, building and deploying multimodal foundation models across the vast biomedical data landscape that will be used within Computational Innovation to enhance and accelerate portfolio decision-making. 

 

THE POSITION 

We are looking for an ML Engineer to join the AI Systems team and contribute to work at the frontier of biomedical AI. This is a hands-on engineering role with real stakes, as the models you help build will be used to make decisions about which indications to pursue, in which patient population and against which target. 

You will work in close partnership with AI scientists and more experienced ML engineers, supporting the translation of validated research prototypes and architectural designs into production-ready implementations at a high engineering standard. You will contribute to early architectural discussions, offering engineering perspectives on training, efficiency, scalability and production-readiness, and iterating with the team on design decisions under senior guidance. 

This is a role for someone who takes pride in engineering craft, who writes clean, well-tested, well-documented code, and who cares that biology retains its integrity as models move from research to production. Your engineering work will go far beyond the model card; it will connect directly to human health outcomes. 

 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Contribute engineering perspectives to architectural design discussions, supporting decisions that ensure foundation models train and infer efficiently and are scalable 
  • Under the guidance of senior ML engineers, implement biomedical foundation model components such as training code, data loaders, tokenisers, inference logic and fine-tuning interfaces to a high engineering standard 
  • Work closely with AI scientists to help translate validated research prototypes into robust, production-quality model artefacts, and contribute to benchmarking and performance evaluation 
  • Contribute to the optimisation of validated models and inference pipelines, applying techniques such as quantisation, distillation and pruning to help meet production efficiency and latency requirements without compromising model performance 
  • Write clean, well-tested, well-documented code and follow the engineering standards set by the team 
  • Support model handovers to MLOps engineers, contributing documentation covering capabilities, known limitations, failure modes and retraining criteria 
  • Stay current with advances in ML engineering, distributed training and biomedical AI tooling 

 

Required Qualifications 

  • Postgraduate degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Computational Biology or a related technical field; PhD preferred or MSc with equivalent industry experience 
  • Hands-on experience with deep learning and foundation model implementations such as transformers, pre-training and fine-tuning 
  • Some experience contributing to production-quality model artefacts, with a growing understanding of what is required to move from research prototypes to reliable deployment 
  • Experience collaborating with researchers during the implementation process 
  • Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch 
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals such as writing clean, testable, well-documented and maintainable code, version control, code reviews 
  • Working knowledge of distributed training frameworks such as PyTorch Distributed, DeepSpeed, FSDP or Ray Train 
  • Exposure to model optimisation techniques for inference, e.g. quantisation, distillation, pruning 

 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience working with biomedical data modalities such as genomics, multi-omics, clinical or imaging data in an ML context is advantageous 
  • Publications or contributions to open-source ML projects or tooling 

 

This is a hybrid role with approximately 3 days a week in the office

+ Ability to structure & prioritise work effectively through close cooperation with the team as a whole

+ Ability to work in a team and independently without losing initiative & focus.

Bispebjerg Hospital in Denmark, Canolfan Pentre Awel in Carmarthen, One Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester, Multi-Megawatt Data Centre Campus, the vast £1 billion Elephant and Castle redevelopment in London, are examples of some of the amazing projects where we have led the design with other Hoare Lea disciplines.

  • Using the latest computer modelling software CAD and Revit

  • Researching ground-breaking technologies
  • Continuous CPD and learning opportunities

About you

  • An expected or achieved 2.1 or above IMechE or CIBSE accredited degree or equivalent qualification in Mechanical Engineering or similar
  • Excellent communication, analytical and organisational skills
  • Ability to work in a team environment and independently
  • A friendly, ambitious and confident individual with a flexible and resilient approach

  • A Masters or other relevant post graduate qualification
  • Previous placement or work experience in a similar industry
  • An understanding of CAD or similar modelling software

jobDescription:
We are looking for an experienced Domestic Gas Engineer to join our highly regarded gas operations and maintenance team based in Brockley and Canning Town, London. This is an exciting opportunity to join a leading FM company where you will be working to complete boiler services (CP12's), fault finding and breakdown repairs in residential properties across our portfolio.

 

Rydon Maintenance is an expanding division of the Rydon Group and is successfully providing facilities management services to a variety of clients, predominantly within the healthcare and housing association sectors. 

We recognise that it’s our people who make Rydon the success it is today and we understand the importance of career development and training. We’re continuously investing in our people and this is what makes us one of the leading employers within the built environment.

 

Watch our careers video to find out more about working for Rydon

 

We are looking for an experienced Domestic Gas Engineer to join our team on a permanent basis. The role is responsible for providing gas/boiler repairs and boiler servicing in domestic properties on a social housing contract.

 

You will be diagnosing and providing repairs to boilers on a reactive call-out basis as well as routine servicing to gas fired boilers (central heating and hot water systems) to ensure they are working to the required quality standards. You will identify any faults and where possible, rectify these during the visit, issuing the completion certificate (CP12) where the systems meet the required safety and quality standards.

 

The role is based in London with the patch covering Brockley and Canning Town. You will be issued with a company van and fuel card as this is a mobile role.

 

Working hours are Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm. You will also participate in our on-call emergency rota, for which you will receive an on-call allowance and overtime rates paid per call out.

 

What we can offer you

 

  • Competitive starting salary.
  • Holiday Entitlement: 25 days per annum
  • Holiday Purchase Scheme: Buy up to an additional 5 days holiday
  • On call allowance and overtime paid per call out.
  • Pension Scheme: 4% contributory.
  • Health Cash Plan: helping you spread the cost of essential healthcare
  • 24/7 EAP Service: free advice, counselling and support for you and your family whenever you need it.
  • Wellbeing and mental health champions readily available at work.
  • Access to an employee discount scheme which includes a wide-range of special offers and discounts on insurances, lifestyle goods and services.
  • Flexible benefits for you to choose from including Critical Illness, DenPlan and Cycle to work schemes.
  • Employee Referral Scheme: recommend a personal connection to us and claim a cash reward for their successful hire.
  • Eye care vouchers ad Free Flu Vaccinations
  • Full training, ongoing coaching and support
  • Opportunities to progress your career across the business

You should have strong experience gained as a domestic gas engineer. This experience would ideally have been gained within a maintenance contractor, though candidates working for an energy provider will also be considered. You should have Domestic ACS qualification; CCN1, CPA1, CKR1, CENWAT, HTR1

 

You’ll be comfortable with undertaking routine servicing as well as repair works across gas fired heating and hot water systems. You will have excellent communication skills and enjoy providing excellent customer services. A keen eye for detail and quality of workmanship is also essential.

 

If this sounds like you, we’d strongly encourage you to apply.

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need motivated and inventive people to join us. If you'd like to help us build the place to find and buy anything online, this is your chance to make history.

The Data Center Global Services team is looking for a Controls Engineer for Construction (BMS/EPMS), responsible for the building automation systems within Amazon data centers to join our EMEA team. If you are passionate about the customer experience, think and act globally and have the ability to contribute to major new innovations in the area of building controls and automation this is the challenge you are looking for!

Our Control Engineers technical background across project/construction management, mechanical, electrical or technology background enable them to undertake the challenges of sophisticated controls platforms to strategically align building controls and automation with the larger objectives of the business. They work individually and as part of a team to develop new products, support existing products, test and evaluate equipment.

Controls Engineers in AWS deploys , maintains BMS(Building Management System) & EPMS(Electrical Power Monitoring System) across our leased/colocation data centers.

They co-ordinate with AWS DCEO( Data Center Engineering Operations) teams to implement new builds, upgrades etc and ensures high availability and high resiliency of these control systems.

Key job responsibilities
Controls Engineers in AWS deploys , maintains BMS(Building Management System) & EPMS(Electrical Power Monitoring System) across our leased/colocation data centers. They co-ordinate with AWS DCEO( Data Center Engineering Operations) teams to implement new builds, upgrades etc and ensures high availability and high resiliency of these control systems.
• Ascertain customer needs to help develop project scope and specifications.
• Manage scopes of work relative to the site specifics and customer needs.
• Manage project engineering to determine the scope of work relative to the design intent of the customer needs.
• Read and interpret specifications and implement those specifications as they apply the work environment.
• Develop control panel BOM’s
• Develop ISA data sheets for temperature, level, flow, and pressure transmitters along with ISA data sheets for control valves, positioners, analytical, and various other types of instrumentation.
• Develop drawings for control panels, power distribution, junction boxes. Included in the drawings are the general arrangement, internal layout, schematics and interconnection and wiring diagrams.
• Develop logic diagrams in the International Automation format for complex logic devices such as Programmable Logical Controller and Distributed Control System. Prepare cable, routing plans and schedules.
• Perform inspections, testing, and commission of the facility systems.
• Coordinate project work internally within the department and externally with other departments to ensure on-time completion of projects within budget.
• Travel domestically and internationally to support other regions


A day in the life
Controls Engineer's day may begin with deployment efforts including on-site site management works , directing Controls vendors for installation / commissioing works and is responsible for quality and on time delivery of the tasks / project. While managing service works, CE will co-ordinate with Operations teams for permits and engages Vendor or performs services confirming to the task lists.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

About the Opportunity

We employ the UK's most experienced and skilled technical services professionals and has grown to over 8,000 people in locations across the UK - we provide the resources to turn great ideas into reality, and we offer capable and committed individuals the opportunity to shape their careers how they wish.

Hinkley Point C (HPC) is the first new nuclear power station to be built in the UK in over 20 years, HPCs two EPR reactors will be capable of generating 3.26GW of secure, low carbon electricity for 60 years, enough electricity to power around 6 million homes. In addition to the projects ‘clean energy’ benefits, HPC will create thousands of jobs and bring lasting benefits to the UK economy.

The Balance of Plant Commissioning Engineer’s role will evolve during the lifecycle of the project and combine technical knowledge with project delivery skills. At the early stages you will contribute to detailed planning and preparation, including reviewing contractor produced

commissioning documentation. Following this, you will execute commissioning tests and conduct surveillance on contractor-led activities as part of a team and analyse the results to justify the readiness of the HPC units to safely enter commercial operation. 

As a Commissioning Engineer you will be responsible for the delivery of test specifications and safety documentation during preparation for commissioning. You will perform site testing safely and effectively, assist with the analysis of commissioning results, resolve problems and take responsibility for ensuring that deliverables supporting HPC commissioning are provided on time, in accordance with the Project’s requirements. This will include giving support to contract partners and taking part in contractual review and acceptance activities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Accountable to a Commissioning Manager in the NNB HPC Project team.  
  • Develop commissioning documentation and review contractor-produced documentation relating to commissioning testing.  
  • Contribute to detailed planning and take ownership of a programme of tests.  
  • Take part in or lead the execution of site commissioning activities which may include supervision of contractor personnel to achieve safe 
  • Commissioning of HPC systems.  
  • Provide information to assist the Commissioning Manager in meeting project-level objectives and milestones.  

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

  • Degree qualified (or equivalent) in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Strong technical knowledge of Mechanical & Process Systems with strong technical engineering skills and problem solving skills
  • Must have good ICT literacy (familiarity with using Excel, using Sharepoint, using Review & Comment functions in Adobe & Word, and adaptability to other software packages used on the project such as Switch/ Fieldview/ Navisworks 3D modelling)
  • Good communication skills and the ability to convey complex information to others and able to work as part of a team and work closely with contractors.

About Linxon

Linxon is a joint venture between Hitachi Energy and SNC-Lavalin, specializing in the engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) delivery of electrical substations and grid infrastructure projects worldwide. At Hinkley Point C, Linxon is responsible for the delivery of critical high-voltage electrical infrastructure supporting the UK's newest nuclear power station.

 

Position Overview

The Construction Manager will lead all site construction activities associated with the delivery of Linxon's electrical balance-of-plant infrastructure at Hinkley Point C. The role is responsible for ensuring safe, efficient, and compliant execution of construction works, including civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical installation activities.

 

The successful candidate will provide leadership to multidisciplinary construction teams and contractors while maintaining alignment with nuclear safety standards, project schedule commitments, quality requirements, and budget objectives.

 

Key Responsibilities

Construction Leadership

  • Lead all onsite construction activities.
  • Drive a strong safety-first culture aligned with HPC and Linxon requirements.
  • Ensure construction works are delivered in accordance with project specifications, programme, quality requirements, and approved methodologies.
  • Coordinate daily site operations across multiple contractors and interfaces.
  • Provide visible leadership and direction to construction supervisors and contractor management teams.


Health, Safety, Environment and Security

  • Promote and uphold the highest standards of health, safety, environmental, and nuclear safety performance.
  • Ensure compliance with CDM Regulations, HPC site rules, permit-to-work systems, and Linxon HSE procedures.
  • Lead construction safety reviews, inspections, audits, and toolbox talks.
  • Investigate incidents and implement corrective and preventive actions.
  • Support achievement of Zero Harm objectives.


Project Planning and Delivery

  • Develop and implement construction execution strategies.
  • Monitor progress against baseline schedules and identify recovery actions where necessary.
  • Coordinate resource planning, logistics, material deliveries, and site access requirements.
  • Participate in schedule reviews and construction readiness assessments.
  • Manage construction risks, constraints, and interface issues.


Contractor Management

  • Manage principal contractors, subcontractors, and specialist installation teams.
  • Monitor contractor performance against safety, quality, productivity, and schedule metrics.
  • Review contractor work packs, RAMS, lift plans, and construction methodologies.
  • Facilitate coordination meetings and drive resolution of construction challenges.
  • Ensure adequate supervision and competency management across all work fronts.


Quality Assurance

  • Ensure all construction works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, ITPs, and quality standards.
  • Support inspection and test activities.
  • Manage punch list closure and handover documentation.
  • Ensure non-conformances are identified, recorded, and resolved effectively.
  • Promote a right-first-time approach to construction execution.


Interface and Stakeholder Management

  • Liaise with HPC delivery teams, EDF stakeholders, designers, commissioning teams, and regulatory representatives.
  • Coordinate interfaces between civil, mechanical, electrical, and commissioning activities.
  • Support project reporting and provide regular updates on construction performance.
  • Represent Linxon in client and stakeholder meetings as required.

 

Commercial and Performance Management

  • Support cost management and forecasting activities.
  • Monitor productivity and resource utilization.
  • Identify change opportunities and constructability improvements.
  • Contribute to project KPI reporting and performance reviews.

 


Qualifications

Essential

  • Degree or HNC/HND in Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline.
  • SMSTS Certification.
  • Strong understanding of Construction Design & Management (CDM) Regulations.
  • Full UK Driving Licence.


Desirable

  • Membership of CIOB, ICE, IET, APM, or equivalent professional body.
  • Nuclear industry qualifications and training.
  • Temporary Works Coordinator certification.
  • NEBOSH Construction Certificate.

 

Experience

Essential

  • Significant experience managing large-scale industrial, infrastructure, power, utility, or energy construction projects.
  • Proven experience delivering HV electrical infrastructure, substations, grid connections, or EPC projects.
  • Experience managing multiple contractors in a highly regulated environment.
  • Demonstrated leadership in achieving high safety performance standards.
  • Experience managing complex construction interfaces and stakeholder relationships.


Desirable

  • Previous nuclear industry experience.
  • Experience working on Hinkley Point C or major UK infrastructure projects.
  • Knowledge of ONR and nuclear quality requirements.

 

What We Offer

  • Opportunity to work on one of Europe's largest and most complex infrastructure projects.
  • Career development within a global EPC organisation.
  • Collaborative and safety-focused working environment.
  • Competitive salary, bonus, pension, and benefits package.

Keep Britain's electricity network moving — and help power the future.

 

National Grid is investing heavily in the UK's electricity transmission network, expanding and modernising substations to meet future energy needs. We're growing our Hertfordshire team and looking for a skilled engineer ready to build a long-term career maintaining some of the country's most critical infrastructure.

Pay and Benefits

  • Salary package £45,137 pa including allowances.
  • Paid overtime + Bonus (2026 – 4%), Company commercial vehicle from home to work.
  • 26 days holiday plus 8 statutory days, Contribution Pension Max Total 18%.
  • Hours - 37 Avg Monday to Friday, Days only (Winter 36 hrs / Summer 38 hrs - 4 day working pattern).
  • For further benefits information please click the link - Benefits | National Grid Careers

Role overview

This hands-on, mechanically biased engineering role involves maintaining, repairing and overhauling the equipment that keeps National Grid's Electricity Transmission substations operating safely and efficiently.

Working predominantly outdoors and sometime at height on a mobile platform, you'll carry out a wide range of maintenance activities including:

  • Stripping, inspecting and rebuilding mechanical components
  • Diagnosing faults and carrying out repairs
  • Replacing worn and ageing components including bearings, seals, fasteners and moving parts
  • Installing new or refurbished equipment
  • Supporting planned maintenance and emergency breakdown response
  • Performing routine inspections and condition monitoring

You'll work on specialist equipment including:

  • Circuit breakers
  • Power transformers
  • High-speed on-load tap changers
  • Air compressor systems
  • Cable systems
  • Ancillary equipment across high-voltage substations.

 

Every day brings new challenges, from rebuilding equipment and aligning components to solving mechanical faults. We'll provide industry-leading training at our Eakring Training Centre in Nottinghamshire, alongside practical site learning, to help you build specialist high-voltage mechanical engineering expertise. Training may include occasional stays away from home, supported by overnight and mobility allowances. Some weekend working is required, with paid overtime available.

Qualifications, Skills and Experience

We're keen to hear from candidates with:

  • A recognised apprenticeship in Mechanical engineering, or an NVQ/Level 3 Mechanical engineering qualification with relevant fitting experience.
  • Strong mechanical maintenance, overhaul or installation experience.
  • Experience stripping, rebuilding and repairing plant and equipment.
  • Confidence using hand tools, power tools, precision measuring equipment and torque tools.
  • A proactive approach to fault finding and problem solving.
  • A strong commitment to safe working practices and can work at height.
  • A full UK driving licence.
  • Confidence using a computer and iPad.
  • You live within approximately 40 minutes travel to Wymondley Substation, SG4 7JJ.

It would be great if you also have:

  • Experience working on high-voltage equipment
  • Previous experience within power generation, utilities, manufacturing, heavy engineering or process industries
  • NEBOSH or IOSH qualifications

 

Please note that visa sponsorship and relocation packages are not available for this role.

 

Build a career that powers the UK

If you want a role where your skills are valued, your development is supported and your work makes a genuine difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Asset Engineer

Business Unit:  National Grid Ventures
Requisition Number:  5404

About the role

 

National Grid Ventures Interconnectors is playing a critical role in connecting the UK's energy system with neighbouring countries, helping to deliver a more secure, resilient and low-carbon energy future. Through our portfolio of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) interconnectors, we enable the import and export of electricity, supporting the UK's transition to net zero while developing the infrastructure needed to meet future energy demands.

 

We're looking for an Asset Engineer to join our Asset & Engineering team. In this role, you'll be responsible for the effective management, performance and maintenance of critical interconnector assets, helping to ensure exceptional levels of reliability, availability and operational resilience across our portfolio.

 

Working closely with site-based and central teams, you'll use your technical expertise to develop asset strategies, drive maintenance excellence, improve asset health and support continuous improvement initiatives. You'll play a key role in ensuring our assets perform safely, efficiently and in line with all regulatory and operational requirements.

 

This position is based at our IFA1 site in Sellindge so candidates would be ideally be based within a hours commute.

What you'll do

 

As an Asset Engineer, you will:

 

  • Deliver asset health assessments and asset management activities in line with National Grid policies and standards.
  • Develop and implement asset maintenance strategies to maximise asset performance, reliability and lifespan.
  • Translate OEM technical guidance and engineering standards into practical maintenance plans, work instructions and Maximo task lists.
  • Produce and manage maintenance plans and outage scopes to ensure maintenance activities are completed safely and effectively.
  • Support the management of asset defects, equipment failures and technical investigations, identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions.
  • Analyse asset performance data and provide recommendations to improve reliability and operational efficiency.
  • Work collaboratively with site operations teams, engineering specialists and external partners to drive best practice across the interconnector portfolio.
  • Coordinate with Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) on warranty, performance and asset integrity matters.
  • Maintain accurate asset records and support continual improvement of asset data within Maximo.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety, compliance and continuous improvement across all engineering activities.

What you'll need

 
  • Experience in engineering and asset management, ideally within the utilities, energy, infrastructure or industrial sectors.
  • Strong understanding of asset management principles and maintenance strategies.
  • Knowledge of high-voltage electrical systems or other critical infrastructure assets.
  • Ability to interpret technical documentation, engineering drawings and OEM manuals.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make informed technical decisions.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Experience using asset management systems such as Maximo or similar platforms.
  • Understanding of risk management processes and regulatory compliance requirements.
  • A proactive approach to continuous improvement and operational excellence.
  • HNC in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering (or equivalent).
  • Full UK Driving Licence.

What you'll get

 

A competitive salary between £47,442.00 - £56,173.50 per annum– dependent on capability.


 As well as your base salary, you will receive a bonus based on personal and company performance and a competitive contributory pension scheme where we will double match your contribution to a maximum company contribution of 12%. You will also have access to a number of flexible benefits such as a share incentive plan, salary sacrifice car and technology schemes, support via employee assistance lines and matched charity giving to name a few.

More Information

 

This role closes on 28th September at 23:59, however we encourage candidates to submit their application as early as possible and not wait until the published closing date as this can vary. 

We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates – we make appointments purely on merit, assessed against objective selection criteria. We support flexible working and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process should you have any physical or mental impairment which may affect your ability to participate in the process.

Please note that in most cases, National Grid is unable to offer sponsorship for employment under the UK points-based immigration system. As such, applicants must have the legal right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship now or in the future under the UK points-based immigration system. However, in exceptional circumstances where there is a clear and demonstrable need for specialist skills that cannot be sourced from the local labour market, National Grid may consider offering sponsorship. All applications are welcome from candidates who meet these requirements, regardless of race, nationality, or ethnic origin.

During the placement you will learn all about what the Calibration department has to offer with a heavy focus on the maintenance world within Airbus and have the opportunity to utilise your skills to work closely with the teams and implement change to solidify our maintenance strategy. The role will put you at the centre of the drilling team supported by dedicated engineers gaining knowledge and understanding of all airbus variants across the site.

You will work with a variety of different people both inside the team and around the plant and will have the opportunity to support and autonomously run projects across Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery and People.

Primary focus will be on the modernising of the maintenance department ranging from the workshop to process improvements on spares management, planned preventive maintenance creating as much opportunity to enable growth into new technologies that we are currently maintaining.

  • Helping with team engagement initiatives and the employee involvement scheme, as well as environment and sustainability projects;

  • You will represent the Calibration business at drumbeat reviews and be a focal point for our customers, which will develop communication, business agility and problem solving skills.

Working with all areas of the business will help develop your presentation, networking and stakeholder management skills that will be required and will be valuable in future career opportunities.

You will also learn about Airbus Operating System's and Lean principles, which will be at the forefront of all the projects to ensure the best possible outcomes can be achieved.

RWE Generation’s Engineering and Outage (E&O) group supports our portfolio of gas-fired power stations across Europe. The Rotating Equipment team is responsible for the technical engineering strategy, performance and risk management for gas turbines and steam turbines within the RWE gas division portfolio. A placement with the Rotating Equipment team will allow you to work within this dynamic and international group of engineers, and will be based either at RWE’s UK head office in Swindon or at one of RWE’s UK power station sites.   • Gain important on-site experience and valuable hands-on practical skills.
  • Enjoy using your problem solving and teamworking skills to successfully deliver your responsibilities.
  • Attend courses, workshops and on the job training for your personal development.

Job Description

As a Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer here at Honeywell, you will lead initiatives to optimize and innovate manufacturing processes, driving operational excellence and efficiency. You will leverage your expertise to implement advanced manufacturing strategies and technologies that enhance productivity and product quality.

The Senior Advanced Manufacturing Engineer will be responsible for developing, implementing, validating, maintaining, and improving manufacturing processes across machining, assembly, test, fabrication, and engineered plastics operations. This role supports the production of centrifugal pump components, including machined metallic components and ANSIMAG sealless magnetic-drive non-metallic product lines with molded ETFE wetted components.

The successful candidate will lead continuous improvement, cost reduction, quality improvement, and production support initiatives by partnering closely with shop-floor technicians, operators, supervisors, Product Engineering, Planning, Quality, Supply Chain, and management. This is a day-shift, salaried position that works under limited supervision and reports to the Shop Supervisor / Manager. You’ll work out of our Arvada, CO location on an On-site work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, validate, maintain, and improve manufacturing processes for assigned areas, including machining, assembly, test, kit fabrication, engineered plastic parts, insert molded parts, and injection molded fabrication processes
  • Create, revise, and maintain NC programs, fixturing, tooling, standard work, process sketches, in-process inspection plans, process notes, assembly instructions, process instructions, test instructions, bills of material, labor routings, and shop-floor routings
  • Evaluate alternative plastic resins, manufacturing methods, equipment, tooling, and process improvements to support cost reduction, manufacturability, quality, and product performance
  • Improve manufacturing efficiency by analyzing workflow, production flow, assembly methods, space requirements, equipment layout, process capability, and production volume while maintaining and improving quality standards
  • Lead analysis of manufacturing costs in support of strategic make/buy decisions, accurate standard costing, capital investment justification, and cost-reduction initiatives
  • Participate in production traceability and configuration control, including changes and corrections to bills of material, routings, technical work instructions, NC programs, inspection plans, and test plans
  • Support non-conforming material disposition, root cause analysis, customer complaint investigations, internal issue resolution, third-party audit responses, and corrective action implementation
  • Lead and support Lean, Six Sigma, TPM, and 5S initiatives to eliminate waste, reduce variation, remove bottlenecks, and improve manufacturing, assembly, test, and fabrication processes
  • Coordinate with Manufacturing Supervision, operators, technicians, engineers, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, and management to resolve production issues and improve manufacturing capabilities
  • Support injection molding training and develop working knowledge of internal processes, customer specifications, and best practices for sealless magnetic-drive pump products
  • Identify, justify, research, quote, procure, test, and implement capital equipment investments, including preparation of Capital Authorization Requests as needed

Qualifications

You Must Have:

  • 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing engineering or similar role within a manufacturing environment
  • 3+ years of experience with CAD/CAM software; Siemens NX preferred
  • 3+ years of experience in machining, metal cutting, plastics manufacturing, injection molding, or related production environment
  • Experience with varied metallurgies such as carbon steel, stainless steel alloys, titanium, Hastelloy, and aluminum preferred
  • Experience supporting engineered plastic components, molded ETFE components, insert molded parts, or injection molded fabrication processes preferred
  • Ability to lift 35 pounds unassisted

We Value

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field
  • Lean Six Sigma experience, APICS certification, or demonstrated experience applying lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies
  • Experience with VPP sites, EH&S programs, TPM, 6S, ISO standard work, and formal safety management practices
  • Experience managing multi-shift or 24-hour machine shop operations
  • Familiarity with various production processes, including plastic molding, tooling, assembly, and test
  • Strong communication skills, reading, listening, and talking are common

The Manufacturing Engineer will support an aerospace sheet metal forming facility in Chandler, AZ by developing efficient, cost-effective manufacturing processes for complex sheet metal components. The role focuses on translating engineering designs, CAD models, specifications, and purchase order requirements into robust production methods, tooling, and process plans that achieve high quality at the lowest practical cost. The engineer will lead and support new product introduction, continuous improvement, and customer liaison activities within an AS9100-regulated environment.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct research and development projects related to the design and development of new products and services, particularly in aerospace sheet metal manufacturing.
  • Contribute to and follow project plans for new product development orders, ensuring tasks progress on schedule and meet technical and quality requirements.
  • Prepare detailed shop operation sketches, instruction sheets, bills of materials, tool orders, and other process documentation to define the most cost-effective integrated fabrication and inspection methods.
  • Review customer documentation and specifications and ensure that all manufacturing plans, routings, and process instructions fully reflect customer requirements.
  • Design and create complete tooling and fixturing drawings using CAD software to support sheet metal fabrication processes, and develop work orders and plans to fabricate tooling either in-house or through outside suppliers.
  • Serve as an engineering liaison with customers, maintaining specific knowledge of customer quality requirements and specifications and communicating effectively to address technical issues and inquiries.
  • Resolve implementation and process problems on the shop floor and respond quickly to liaison requests related to manufacturing issues.
  • Provide technical assistance to shop and inspection personnel, perform MRB (Material Review Board) dispositions, and conduct investigations to resolve quality and process problems.
  • Maintain close working relationships with all departments and individuals involved in assigned projects and coordinate with customer representatives as necessary to support program success.
  • Monitor manufacturing cell metrics, including gross margin, scrap, rework, 5S, and other continuous improvement indicators, and identify improvement opportunities with actionable plans to address them.
  • Conduct special studies to develop and establish standard hours, cost data, and other metrics to support cost reduction and productivity improvement initiatives.
  • Consult with clients, vendors, and other stakeholders to discuss and formulate estimates, clarify requirements, and resolve technical or process issues.
  • Create and maintain process layouts and routings, ensuring accurate and efficient workflow definitions for 3–7 years of experience in this area.
  • Apply GD&T principles in daily work to ensure accurate interpretation and communication of dimensional and tolerance requirements on drawings and process documents.
  • Use lean tools such as Six Sigma and value stream mapping (VSM) to identify and implement process improvements across manufacturing cells.
  • Support or participate in multi-axis programming activities, such as laser cutting or other CNC processes, where applicable.
  • Perform all other related duties as assigned to support production, engineering, and continuous improvement objectives.

Essential Skills

  • Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Engineering, or at least seven (7) years of related experience, or a combination of education and experience in a manufacturing environment focused on exotic sheet metal, preferably in aerospace.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in manufacturing engineering, tooling design, and manufacturing process development for metal forming and aerospace sheet metal components; candidates without a degree may require 10–15 years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with sheet metal fabrication methods such as hydroforming, heat treat, brazing, laser cutting, brake forming, welding (TIG and resistance), and NDT processes; in some roles, at least seven (7) years of experience with these methods is required.
  • Proficiency in sheet metal manufacturing methods using metals such as aluminum, nickel alloys, stainless steels, and titanium, with at least seven (7) years of experience in these materials in certain positions.
  • Strong CAD modeling experience, including designing tools and fixtures for sheet metal forming; candidates should have at least seven (7) years of CAD experience and be able to rate their CAD ability at 7/10 or higher.
  • Ability to design tooling for sheet metal forming using CAD, with a minimum of three (3) years of experience with a BS degree or seven (7) years without a degree.
  • Daily, practical command of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing), demonstrated through consistent use in recent work experience.
  • Experience in process layout and routing creation, typically 3–7 years of hands-on work defining and documenting manufacturing processes.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Project, for documentation, reporting, and project management.
  • Familiarity with ERP systems for managing bills of materials, routings, work orders, and related production data.
  • Understanding and practical use of lean tools such as Six Sigma and value stream mapping (VSM), with at least seven (7) years of experience using these tools in some roles.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journals, financial reports, legal documents, and customer specifications.
  • Ability to respond professionally to inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community.
  • Ability to effectively present information to immediate supervisors and upper management, both verbally and in writing.
  • Strong mathematical skills, including probability, statistical inference, plane and solid geometry, and trigonometry, applied to manufacturing and process engineering problems.
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, draw valid conclusions, and interpret complex technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form while managing both abstract and concrete variables.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

  • Experience in an aerospace sheet metal manufacturing environment, particularly with exotic metals and complex formed components.
  • Experience with CAD platforms such as SolidWorks, NX, or comparable 3D CAD programs for modeling parts, tools, and fixtures.
  • Experience with multi-axis programming, ideally for laser cutting equipment, though programming experience on other multi-axis machines is also valuable.
  • Background in process engineering, machining, and fixture design to support integrated manufacturing solutions.
  • Experience with heat treat processes and their integration into overall manufacturing process flows.
  • Familiarity with press brake and roll forming operations for aerospace sheet metal components.
  • Experience with Mastercam or similar CAM software for programming machining or cutting operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage project plans and move work forward proactively without waiting for detailed direction at each step.
  • Experience working within AS9100 or similar quality management systems in aerospace or other highly regulated industries.
  • Exposure to continuous improvement initiatives, including 5S and lean manufacturing cell development.
  • Comfort working with clients, vendors, and cross-functional teams to align technical requirements and resolve issues efficiently.

Work Environment

The role is based in an aerospace sheet metal forming contract manufacturing facility operating under AS9100 regulations. The environment centers on the production of complex components made from exotic metals such as aluminum, nickel alloys, stainless steel, and titanium using processes like hydroforming, heat treat, brazing, laser cutting, brake forming, welding (TIG and resistance), NDT, press brake, and roll forming. The Manufacturing Engineer will work closely with production, quality, and inspection teams on the shop floor and in an office setting, using CAD software (such as SolidWorks, NX, or similar), ERP systems, Microsoft Office, and potentially CAM tools like Mastercam. The facility emphasizes lean manufacturing, 5S, and continuous improvement within manufacturing cells, with a strong focus on meeting aerospace quality and regulatory requirements. The organization is growing, adding new programs and customers, and investing in infrastructure and people, offering a dynamic environment with significant opportunities to contribute to new product introductions and long-term program growth.

Develops, implements, and improves manufacturing and industrial processes to effect maximum product throughput and optimum resource efficiency. Works closely with other engineers and other functional departments to ensure schedule, systems, and part/process data integrity.

Manufacturing Engineer ALL

  • Works with customer released or KUAS released drawings and/or CAD models, engineering BOMs, and other engineering specifications to develop, implement and improve manufacturing processes.

  • Responsible for disposition of discrepant or non-conforming product.
  • Has familiarity with CAD tools, manufacturing execution systems, ERP, and other commonly used software.
  • Designs, coordinates and validates workstation layouts with an emphasis on ergonomics, single piece or small batch flow, visual aids, Poke Yoke (mistake proofing), 5S, and zero-defect policies.

Role Purpose

The Automation Engineer is responsible for the reliability, safety, optimisation, and continuous improvement of industrial automation and control systems within Danish Crown’s food manufacturing environment.

The role ensures stable and compliant operation of automated production and utility systems in line with food safety, quality, and health & safety requirements. The position works closely with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, and IT. IT infrastructure and enterprise systems remain owned by the IT function; this role provides operational input, coordination, and system expertise to support them.

Key Responsibilities

Automation & Production Systems

  • Develop, maintain, and optimise PLC, HMI, SCADA, and MES‑related automation systems supporting production performance (e.g. OEE, SAP PM interfaces).
  • Troubleshoot automation, electrical, and process control issues across production and utilities.
  • Ensure high availability and reliable performance of automated equipment in a regulated food environment.
  • Act as the production automation interface to IT by providing requirements, impact assessments, testing support, and coordination for system changes.

Food Safety, Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure automation solutions comply with HACCP, hygienic design principles, and Danish Crown standards.
  • Support QEHS compliance, legal obligations, and internal governance.
  • Participate in risk assessments, validation, and controlled change processes for automation changes.

Continuous Improvement & Reliability

  • Drive CI initiatives targeting efficiency, uptime, yield, and waste reduction.
  • Apply RCA, FMECA, RCM, and CBM methods to reduce recurring failures.
  • Support LEAN ways of working, site performance boards, and problem‑solving routines.

CAPEX & Project Delivery

  • Provide automation input to CAPEX projects including scope definition, functional specifications, commissioning, and handover.
  • Coordinate with IT where projects affect IT‑managed systems.
  • Manage suppliers, system integrators, and contractors within the automation scope.

Maintenance & Technical Governance

  • Support specialist automation maintenance activities and standards.
  • Develop and maintain SOPs and work instructions.
  • Act as CMMS (SAP PM) super‑user from an automation and maintenance perspective.
  • Support design reviews, upgrades, and obsolescence management.

Collaboration & Capability Building

  • Work closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, quality, and IT teams.
  • Train and coach operators and technicians in automation systems and process optimisation.
  • Support peer‑site collaboration and external supplier engagement.

Required Education & Experience

  • Degree in Automation, Electrical, Mechanical, or Process Engineering or a relevant technical apprenticeship with strong automation specialisation.
  • Experience in automation or engineering roles within food, FMCG, or regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Hands‑on experience with PLC, HMI, SCADA, MES environments and CMMS systems (preferably SAP PM).

Technical Knowledge & Competencies

  • Strong understanding of HACCP, hygienic design, and food manufacturing constraints.
  • Experience with reliability engineering and LEAN principles.
  • Structured problem‑solving, strong communication skills, and the ability to challenge constructively.
  • Solid digital literacy and ability to work effectively alongside IT‑owned systems.

Location: London - Hybrid

Role Summary

Nebula is Pearson’s enterprise Product Design System: a shared platform of reusable components, semantic tokens, standards, tooling, and governance that enables product teams to build high-quality, accessible, brand-aligned and AI-ready experiences faster.

Pearson has already demonstrated the value of this model through PLS, including measurable reductions in component-development effort, embedded WCAG 2.2 accessibility, and faster enterprise-wide change. The next challenge is scaling Nebula from a successful system into a durable enterprise capability adopted across Pearson’s products and business units.

As Principal Product Manager for Nebula , you are the senior product leader responsible for turning Nebula’s enterprise vision into an outcome-driven platform roadmap, adoption strategy, and measurable business value .

You partner closely with the Director of Design Systems , who leads Nebula’s system vision, experience and craft strategy, standards, governance, and design/engineering capability. Together, you operate Nebula as an enterprise product—not a component library or downstream service.

Your focus is to make sure Pearson is building the right shared capabilities, for the right consuming teams, in the right sequence—and that adoption produces measurable value.

What You Own

1. Enterprise Product Strategy & Roadmap

Translate Nebula’s enterprise vision into an evidence-led product strategy and prioritized multi-year roadmap.

You will:

  • Co-own the enterprise Nebula roadmap with the Design Systems Director, translating system strategy into product outcomes, initiatives and sequencing.

  • Define the problems Nebula should solve across Pearson’s business units and product portfolios.

  • Prioritize investments across reusable components, platform capabilities, adoption tooling, AI-enabled workflows, Platinum/brand integration and emerging Content/AI needs.

  • Establish clear product hypotheses, success measures and decision criteria before major investments.

  • Balance enterprise standardization against legitimate product and technical differences across consuming teams.

  • Maintain a transparent roadmap connecting investment capabilities adoption measurable enterprise value.

2. Adoption Product Strategy & BU Onboarding

Treat adoption as a product problem , not a communications or change-management exercise.

You will:

  • Segment Pearson products and business units by readiness, compatibility, value opportunity and migration complexity.

  • Partner with BU Product and Engineering leaders to turn interested teams into roadmap-committed adopters with named products, dates, owners and scope .

  • Lead discovery with consuming teams to understand adoption friction, unmet platform needs and migration barriers.

  • Design the end-to-end Nebula adoption experience: evaluation commitment onboarding migration contribution ongoing consumption.

  • Define scalable pilots and onboarding models before expanding enterprise-wide.

  • Use adoption feedback to shape platform roadmap priorities.

  • Partner with Program Management on intake and migration sequencing while retaining product accountability for what and why .

3. Outcomes, Telemetry & Value Measurement

Own the evidence that proves Nebula is working.

You will:

  • Establish the Nebula measurement framework with leading and lagging indicators.

  • Define telemetry for:

  • active products using Nebula

  • component reuse

  • avoided bespoke rebuilds

  • adoption and migration velocity

  • accessibility readiness

  • design-to-code fidelity

  • rebrand propagation time

  • product-development capacity released

  • Create dashboards that allow the central team, BU teams and executives to see adoption and value.

  • Validate assumptions in the business case against real adoption data.

  • Use evidence to stop, change or accelerate investments.

  • Build the product-level evidence required to continuously strengthen Nebula’s enterprise investment case.

4. Discovery & Platform Customer Insight

Build continuous discovery into the operation of the design system.

Your “customers” include designers and engineers, but also Product leaders, accessibility teams, AI teams, Brand, and business units consuming the platform.

You will:

  • Run ongoing generative and evaluative discovery with consuming teams.

  • Identify recurring problems that should become shared enterprise capabilities rather than local solutions.

  • Determine where standardization creates leverage and where flexibility is required.

  • Validate high-value component, workflow and platform opportunities before committing significant central-team capacity.

  • Create feedback mechanisms that allow BU contributions and needs to flow back into Nebula.

  • Turn qualitative customer insight and telemetry into roadmap decisions.

The original Principal PM role’s strength in continuous discovery should stay; its purpose simply shifts from coaching other PMs to directly improving Nebula.

5. Prioritization & Product Operating Model

Create the product discipline that allows a specialized platform team to make high-quality trade-offs.

You will:

  • Own Nebula prioritization and outcome-based backlog management.

  • Establish clear criteria for:

  • platform investments

  • component requests

  • migrations

  • contribution proposals

  • exceptions

  • enterprise versus BU-specific work

  • Partner with the Director, Principal Engineer and discipline leads on roadmap and release planning.

  • Ensure roadmap commitments reflect available team capacity and enterprise value.

  • Convert ambiguous enterprise asks into appropriately sized discovery and delivery increments.

  • Maintain decision traceability from customer problem investment outcome.

The Head of Customer Advocacy will lead advisory boards, customer advocacy programs, consortium initiatives, evidence generation efforts, claims validation processes, and customer reference strategies while partnering closely with Product Marketing, Commercial Strategy, Clinical, Product Management, Communications, Regional Marketing, Regional Sales, Strategic Partnership Managers (SPMs), and Executive Leadership teams.
The role will serve as a central point of coordination between global marketing teams and customer-facing field organizations to ensure customer advocacy, evidence generation, and collaborative innovation initiatives support both global strategy and regional commercial priorities.

Are you passionate about transforming customer relationships into strategic business impact? In this highly visible global role, you'll partner with leading oncology organisations, clinicians, executives, and internal stakeholders to build advocacy programmes, advisory boards, evidence-generation initiatives, and customer communities that directly influence product strategy, commercial growth, and the future of cancer care technology.

An accomplished Product Delivery Lead is required to join the Willis Neuron product team. You will own delivery of a set of Risk & Analytics features within Willis Neuron, part of a broader portfolio of strategic technology delivery across the group. We are looking for a team member to bring expertise in all areas of product management, from supporting the early development of opportunities through to delivery. jobDescription:
Who We Are

Atwell, LLC is a bold leader in the consulting, engineering, and construction services industry, delivering a broad range of creative solutions to clients in the real estate & land development, and energy markets. We have a strong national presence and a diverse, award-winning project portfolio. Atwell is a privately owned company, with 2,000+ passionate team members across 75+ locations and growing!

Atwell, LLC is a proud recipient of the following 2025 awards:

  • Ten consecutive years in a row as a “Best Place to Work” by Zweig Group (#11)
  • Recognized as #70 in the ENR Top 500 Design Firms, ranked in every region
  • Recognized in Crain's “Fast 50” as one of the fastest-growing companies (#14)
  • Recognized as the 2025 ENR Design Firm of the year for the Southeastern US

Position Snapshot: Civil/Structural Engineer – Oil & Gas

Atwell is seeking a licensed Civil/Structural Engineer (PE) with experience supporting structural design and engineering for the Oil and Gas industry. Our current project portfolio includes oil and natural gas, CO₂, hydrogen, and renewable natural gas (RNG) pipelines, terminals, compressor stations, and processing facilities.

In this role, you will be responsible for leading and executing civil and structural engineering efforts, ensuring alignment with project scope, schedule, budgets, client expectations, and applicable codes and standards. This position involves developing engineering documentation from concept through construction, overseeing structural analyses, mentoring junior team members, and coordinating across disciplines to support successful project execution.

You will play a critical role in the design of reinforced concrete foundations, structural steel platforms and supports, equipment skids, and pipeline structural systems.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Lead the civil and structural engineering design for oil and gas infrastructure projects, including pipelines, pump stations, compressor stations, terminals, and process facilities
  • Develop construction documents, including structural plans, general arrangements, framing plans, and connection details for steel and concrete structures
  • Support the design and coordination of ductwork systems within oil and gas facilities, including duct routing, equipment interfaces, structural supports, and coordination with piping, mechanical, and electrical disciplines
  • Conduct structural analysis under various loading conditions including wind, seismic, blast, and equipment loads in accordance with applicable codes (IBC, ASCE, AISC, ACI, API, etc.)
  • Review and approve engineering calculations, drawings, and reports prepared by internal teams and subcontractors
  • Collaborate with multidiscipline teams including mechanical, piping, and electrical to coordinate structural requirements across project phases
  • Perform field visits to verify as-built conditions, gather site data, and provide construction support as needed
  • Provide mentorship to junior engineers and support team development through technical leadership
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets, and resource allocations to ensure deliverables are met on time and within scope
  • Support quality assurance by implementing Atwell’s QA/QC procedures and best practices

Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering from an ABET-accredited institution (Master’s a plus)
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license required
  • 7+ years of experience in civil/structural engineering for oil and gas facilities or similar industrial infrastructure
  • Proficient in structural analysis software such as STAAD.Pro, RISA, SAP2000, or similar
  • Working knowledge of CAD software tools including AutoCAD, CADWorx, and Civil 3D
  • Familiarity with Autodesk Inventor, Navisworks, or Tekla Structures is a plus
  • Strong knowledge of applicable design codes: AISC, ACI, ASCE, API, IBC
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook)

Pay Range - $100,000 - $150,000 base+, + end of year bonus. 

Disclaimer 

While AI tools may support your application process, this role is built on human talent. Your judgment, experience, and character matter most, so we encourage you to showcase what makes you uniquely you.

Atwell does not accept unsolicited resumes from any 3rd party agencies. No fee will be paid to 3rd parties who submit unsolicited resumes to any Atwell employee. Resumes from approved vendors must be specifically requested by Atwell and approved by the Atwell Talent Acquisition Team.

Pay Range : $100,000 USD - $150,000 USD

Atwell Benefits: To attract and retain the best professionals in the industry, we aim to provide an excellent working environment and a progressive benefits program designed to support your personal and professional needs.

Work/Life:

  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Flexible work schedules are available for some positions
  • Tenure Awards — Travel Vouchers to see the world based on your travel preferences

Compensation:

  • Competitive Compensation packages 
  • Annual bonuses, spot bonuses and peer recognition awards
  • 401K match - 1:1 up to 4% of compensation 
  • Tuition Assistance
  • Student Loan Repayment 
  • Paid Licensing / Certification Fees and Renewals
  • Financial Rewards for Obtaining Licensure
  • Employee Referrals 
  • Annual Wellness Reimbursement for anything wellness related (Gym memberships, fitness tracker, home gym equipment, etc.)
  • Dependent Care Match

‘Atwell’ness:

  • Medical (BC/BS), Dental (Delta), and Vision (VSP)
  • Family Planning & IVF Benefits
  • Pet Insurance
  • Health Savings Account & Flex Spending Account options
  • Employer paid LTD, STD, and life insurance
  • Metlife Supplemental Benefits covering accident, hospitalization, and critical illness
  • Member Assistance Program (MAP) with complimentary counseling sessions, legal benefits, financial consultations, and work/life referral services

At EXP, we’re driven to provide innovative solutions for the world’s built and natural environments. Are you ready to design your future?

  • Structural design for all project types, including complex bridges;

  • Perform analysis and design calculations according to the applicable design codes; use computer programs as appropriate;

Job Description

Join us in preserving engineering heritage while pioneering the future of resilient water infrastructure! You will help to deliver industry-leading reservoir and dam projects across the UK and further afield, including safety upgrades, hydropower, new storage and resilience schemes.

Our graduates gain valuable experience working on a variety of projects alongside a multitude of different disciplines. Our graduates are encouraged to develop their understanding of many elements within the water industry, such as hydraulic, structural, geotechnical and environmental design through calculations, report writing and use of engineering software. You will work alongside our experienced engineers and consultants as you develop these skills within a positive culture where learning and development is actively supported and promoted.

_Here’s what you’ll do:_

+ Undertake numerical analysis including the use of specialist software to assist with the study of dams and reservoirs

+ Keep up-to-date with developments in regulatory legislation and guidelines that may affect design work

+ Carry out research and apply your theoretical knowledge to new situations, assisting with the continuous improvement of our project delivery

+ Undertake feasibility studies to appraise the practicability of alternative solutions, including considerations such as technical performance, health and safety, cost, environmental benefits

+ Prepare designs, drawings, specifications and contracts

+ Write clear, concise reports and prepare presentations for colleagues, clients and regulators

+ Join site visits to support dam inspections and broaden your understanding of how assets perform in the real world.

_Examples of projects we’re working on:_

+ Exploring potential locations for new reservoirs across the Southwest—helping clients plan long-term resilience in the face of climate change.

+ Designing eight dams as part of the Loch Kemp pumped storage hydro scheme—supporting the energy transition with large-scale, flexible low-carbon infrastructure.

+ Upgrading ageing dams to maintain safety and performance, including historic lakes with significant heritage value—balancing safety, sustainability, and cultural importance.

+ Helping clients across the UK maintain safe dams and compliance with the Reservoirs Act 1975, including carrying out statutory inspections, designing upgrades and planning for emergencies.

+ Supporting our colleagues in the USA with the risk assessment of a portfolio of dams, helping to understand the key areas where works can deliver improvements in dam safety.

+ Water-related modules or relevant work experience would be an advantage.

+ Enthusiastic, hard-working and technically proficient.

+ Curiosity and an inquisitive mindset, with strong research skills.

+ Interest in reservoir engineering and the wider water industry.

+ Good written and verbal communication skills, considering technical stakeholders, clients and members of the public.

+ Structure & prioritise work effectively through close cooperation with multi-disciplinary teams.

+ Work independently with initiative to deliver high-quality outputs.

+ An interest in applying sustainable development principles across your work.

Capability to consider client and business expectations and be able to consider the wider financial and commercial implications of your actions.

Job Title:  Project Engineer

Country/Region:  Ireland

Murphy is recruiting a Project Engineer to support our expanding Water & Wastewater portfolio, delivering full design‑to‑operation solutions for Uisce Éireann, Northern Ireland Water and other key clients, underpinned by our commitment to delivering safely, responsibly and to the highest standards.

 

We are looking for a technically strong Senior Project Engineer to provide specialist engineering input and technical leadership on complex clean water and/or wastewater infrastructure projects, and sludge treatment and bioresources. This role focuses on the detailed technical aspects of project delivery — including design development, optioneering, technical assurance, and problem resolution — supporting the UK water sector’s AMP investment programmes. You will work as a key team member within multi-disciplinary teams, ensuring schemes meet regulatory, safety, performance, and sustainability standards.

 

What you will be doing:

  • Develop and optimise technical designs for water and wastewater projects, including treatment works upgrades, network reinforcements, pumping stations, process improvements, and sludge treatment facilities.
  • Lead technical optioneering, hydraulic and process modelling, scheme appraisals, and detailed engineering calculations from concept through to construction-ready stage, with input on sludge handling processes.
  • Provide high-level technical assurance and review of designs, specifications, drawings (including P&IDs), and contractor submissions.
  • Resolve complex technical queries and engineering challenges during design, construction, and commissioning phases.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant standards, regulations (e.g., DWI, EA, Ofwat), CDM 2015, company engineering specifications, and health & safety requirements.
  • Support site-based activities, including technical site inspections, testing (FAT/SAT), commissioning oversight, and handover documentation.
  • Collaborate closely with design teams, contractors, and stakeholders to integrate MEICA (Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control & Automation) elements effectively.
  • Contribute to innovation, digital delivery (BIM, GIS), sustainability initiatives (including net-zero and bioresource optimisation), and value engineering from a technical perspective.
  • Prepare and review technical reports, briefs, risk registers (technical elements), and assurance documentation, with focus on sludge process performance and environmental compliance.

 

Who we are looking for:

  • Degree (or equivalent) in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Process, or Environmental Engineering (or closely related discipline).
  • Minimum 2–5 years’ relevant post-graduate experience in the UK water industry, with strong technical delivery on capital projects (clean water, wastewater treatment, or infrastructure), including demonstrable knowledge and experience of sludge treatment processes.
  • Sound knowledge of water/wastewater processes, hydraulic design, sludge treatment technologies and industry standards/regulations.
  • Experience of technical design development, optioneering, and assurance processes
  • Understanding of CDM 2015 and health & safety in a construction/environmental context (IOSH Managing Safely or equivalent).
  • Working towards or holding Chartered Engineer (CEng) status with ICE, CIWEM, IMechE, IChemE, or IET.
  • Experience across AMP programmes and with major water utilities or consultancies, particularly in bioresources and sludge optimisation.
  • Familiarity with MEICA systems, process safety, hydraulic/process modelling tools, BIM Level 2, and digital engineering applied to sludge facilities. 

What you will get in return

  •  27 days holiday, plus bank holidays with the option to buy an additional 2 days holiday each year, holidays increase with length of service

  • Above market rate contributory pension scheme

Join SP Energy Networks as a Project Engineer (Design) and play a vital role in shaping the future of our district distribution network.   • Relevant network construction and operational experience that gives you practical insight into how designs translate to real-world infrastructure
  • Thorough knowledge of design standards up to 11kV

  • Developed skills with network evaluation modelling tools, enabling you to devise solutions to complex problems and requirements
  • General commercial awareness with the ability to balance customer service, efficient network design, and maximum return on investment
  • Effective stakeholder and customer service engagement skills
  • Ability to communicate and present information clearly at all levels of the organization
  • Capability to manage multiple priorities using sound engineering and financial judgement to identify optimal solutions
  • Awareness of key business drivers and the external commercial context in which ScottishPower operates
  • Computer literacy to work with various digital tools and systems daily
  • Ability to make balanced judgements, taking into account all available information, consulting with others when applicable, and anticipating possible outcomes
  • Technical and operational experience that enables you to plan effectively and contribute meaningfully to team goals

What's in it for you


As well as an attractive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we'll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.

At ScottishPower, we believe it's the little things we do in life that make a big difference. SP Energy Networks is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world's largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. We keep electricity flowing to homes and businesses through Central and Southern Scotland, North Wales and in the North West of England. We operate over 4000km of cables and lines that make-up the transmission network - connecting infrastructure like wind farms into the electricity system. It's a role that puts us right at the heart of Scotland's ambition to be Net Zero by 2044. And we're taking it very seriously. There has never been a more important time to join Southern Water. As we move through AMP8, we are delivering one of the most ambitious capital investment programmes in the industry, focused on improving environmental performance, service resilience and long‑term affordability for customers.

 

About the role

 

The Project Engineer (Rising Main Performance & Condition-Based Maintenance) is responsible for improving the reliability and resilience of rising mains across the region through the integrated analysis of operational, telemetry, and condition-based maintenance (CBM) datasets.

 

The role combines hydraulic and data-driven insight to identify emerging failure risks, including transient pressures, asset deterioration, pump performance issues, and system instability, and proactively develops intervention plans designed to prevent bursts and failures before they occur.

 

What you will be responsible for

  • You will be accountable for defining appropriate intervention strategies for individual rising mains, working closely with operational, asset, and engineering stakeholders to agree solutions, and overseeing contractors responsible for delivering site interventions
  • Analyse analytical platform outputs and telemetry datasets to identify pressure transients, abnormal operating conditions, and emerging risks on rising mains. 
  • Develop and run data-led models of rising main behaviour to determine likely root causes of abnormal operation, including pump control interactions, transient events, and system constraints.
  • Engage, brief, and oversee contractors responsible for implementing agreed calming and control solutions, ensuring works are delivered safely, effectively, and to specification.

What you’ll bring to the role

  • Strong experience working with complex analytical or telemetry datasets within an engineering, asset, or operational context.
  • Proven ability to interpret data to diagnose performance issues and failure modes.
  • Experience developing technical recommendations based on quantitative evidence.
  • Ability to work across multiple teams, including operations, engineering, and external contractors.
  • Understanding of rising main operation, transient pressures, and pump controls.
